ops.title: Abstention over the cc-notes corpus is not solvable with lexical or graph signals (2026-07-27)
ops.body:
Phase 2 tested six model-free abstention signals against the 7 unanswerable of 42 monorepo questions, scored by AUC with a Hanley-McNeil standard error.

  graphEntropy   AUC 0.286 (inverted 0.714) SE 0.096   <- best
  graphCount     AUC 0.412 (inverted 0.588) SE 0.114
  graphTop       AUC 0.439 (inverted 0.561) SE 0.117
  laneAgreement  AUC 0.439 (inverted 0.561) SE 0.117
  lexAbsolute    AUC 0.547 (inverted 0.453) SE 0.123
  lexMargin      AUC 0.608 (inverted 0.392) SE 0.123

The graph does beat the lexical baseline the previous phase measured (0.514) — graphEntropy's 0.714 +/- 0.096 has a 95 percent CI of roughly [0.52, 0.90], so it is only barely distinguishable from chance at n=7 positives. The operating points settle it: the best threshold catches 4 of 7 unanswerable questions while withholding 11 of 35 answerable ones (precision 27 percent), and loosening it to catch 5 costs 14 withheld. Nothing shippable.

Why: the traps are the topically nearest record by construction (q040 asks for a hit rate the sccache notes are dense with the vocabulary for; q044's task title contains exactly the actions asked about). Both lanes rank them first because they ARE the closest records. The missing predicate is whether the specific fact asked for exists, which is an entailment question no ranking signal answers.

The ranker therefore ships no abstention decision. Leak stays at 0.055 (the supersede gate's contribution, down from bm25's 0.100); the abstention-category leak is 0.086 across every configuration measured, unmoved by lane, weight, or normalization.
